envelope.text: a freestanding image has no argv, so the name is absent there

why:
phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `Context::new(args: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl AsRef<str>>, options: InitOptions) -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:293`), HOSTED ONLY (`#[cfg(feature = "env")]`): `Context::new(std::env::args(), InitOptions::new())` compiles as written (`AsRef<str>` is a superset of rclrs's `Item = String`; `context_new_accepts_rclrs_argv_shape`).

ADOPT-BOUNDED, two bounds, both stated in the doc comment. (1) The PLATFORM CONSTRAINT: a freestanding image has no argv, so the name is ABSENT there and the compiler says so — `no function or associated item named new`; the constructors that exist on every target are `default_from_env` / `from_env`. (2) The argument contract: rclrs PARSES `--ros-args` (remaps, parameter overrides); ours does not parse them and does not silently drop them either. The refusal is the RUNTIME refuse-loud site: `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:298` calls `refuse_ros_args` (`:464-471`, the ONE site shared with `init_with_args`), which scans with `args_have_ros_args` (`:451`, exact match) and on a hit logs `REFUSE_INIT_ARGS` (`:433`) through `nros_log` and panics with the same text — the shape `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` has in `rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp`. A vector with no ROS arguments passes through to `from_env(options)` untouched, because nothing was dropped. Tests: `context_new_refuses_ros_args` (`#[should_panic(expected = "--ros-args")]`), `context_new_passes_plain_args_through`.

Not `refuse-loud` as the disposition, deliberately: that word is for a name that EXISTS ONLY to refuse. This name works — with default options, with a domain override, with a plain argv — and refuses one VALUE; the value-level refusal is what `adopt-bounded`'s envelope carries, and the parse of `--ros-args` is still owed beside `nros::resolve_name` (RFC-0020 class 4), recorded on `rust:init_with_args`.

History: `gap` + `absent` (phase-428 Q1, then kept by the closure survey, which found it is not a `rename` of `init_with_args`); decided 2026-09-07 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled") and landed.

phase-467 Row 11 (2026-10-03) -- bound (2) CHANGED: it now PARSES. `-r`/`--remap` rules inside `--ros-args` are honoured (carried on the `Context`, installed by `create_executor{,_in}` as the fallback remap tier, launch rules win); every other ROS argument is refused loudly with the argument named. One parse shared with `init_with_args` (`parse_ros_args_or_refuse`), pinned equal by `context_new_parses_exactly_like_init_with_args`. `context_new_refuses_ros_args` became `context_new_refuses_what_it_cannot_honour` (`--enclave`), because refusing `-r` is no longer the contract. The full envelope is on `rust:init_with_args`, which also carries the one residue both names share -- `-p` parameter overrides, still refused -- as its `owed` witness. This row stays `divergence` because its OTHER bound (no argv on a freestanding image) is the platform constraint it was filed for.
